comment: Every feature this fork carries over pingdotgg/t3code. Each entry's "keep" line is the per-file resolution rule an upstream merge conflict is settled by: what of ours must survive in the listed files, and what takes upstream. scripts/check-fork-features.ts fails when a keep line, a listed file or a test file is gone, then runs the listed tests. .github/workflows/fork-update.yml runs it in the gate, so an upstream merge that deletes a fork seam stops before it can publish. See docs/agents/upstream-conflict-resolution.md and docs/operations/fork-windows-build.md.

features.name: fork-app-identity
features.description: The fork installs and runs beside official T3 Code: its own app id, product name, state directory (~/.t3-fork) and t3code-fork:// URL scheme. Issues #34 and #59.
features.keep: Our app id, product name, window title, ~/.t3-fork state directory, t3code-fork:// URL scheme and Linux desktop entry name and WM class replace upstream's wherever these files set them; take upstream for the rest of these files, then re-apply those settings on top.

features.name: fork-desktop-build
features.description: The desktop build stages the fork's app id, product name and installer file name, and reads its update source from T3CODE_DESKTOP_UPDATE_REPOSITORY. scripts/release-smoke.ts also carries the fork's fix for running the release-only shell steps under Git for Windows bash. Issues #59, #75 and #94.
features.keep: Our app id, product name, installer file name, the T3CODE_DESKTOP_UPDATE_REPOSITORY update source and the Git for Windows bash fix in release-smoke.ts replace upstream's; take upstream for the rest of these files, then re-apply those parts on top.

features.name: windows-console-suppression
features.description: Spawned server and provider processes no longer draw a console window on Windows. Issue #82.
features.keep: windowsConsole.ts is ours whole; take upstream for the rest of the other listed files, then re-apply every call into windowsConsole.ts that hides a spawned console window on top.

features.name: terminal-subprocess-poll
features.description: Bounded terminal and preview polling on one shared back-off engine: a probe budget held under the poll period, bounded fan-out, a round that backs off when nothing changed and returns to the base period on any event. Issue #83, merged in #106, re-applied on upstream v0.0.39's terminal manager in #125. pollLoop.ts is the fork's own module and upstream has no file at that path, so its test cannot pass on plain upstream.
features.keep: pollLoop.ts is ours whole, and Manager.ts and PortScanner.ts must still drive their polling through it; take upstream for the rest of those two files, then re-apply the pollLoop call sites on top.

features.name: fork-automatic-updates
features.description: A found update downloads with no click and installs on the next quit. One update pill label names the waiting version, Settings shows the state in plain words, and a switch turns it off for upstream's two-click flow. forkAutomaticUpdates.ts and forkAutomaticUpdates.logic.ts are the fork's own modules and upstream has no file at either path, so the test cannot pass on plain upstream. Issue #113.
features.keep: forkAutomaticUpdates.ts and forkAutomaticUpdates.logic.ts are ours whole, and the automatic download, the single update pill label, the Settings state and switch, and the IPC channel that carries them survive in the other listed files; the "Update pill label" row in docs/internals/glossary.md is ours whole too; everything else in those files takes upstream.

features.name: fork-repository-identity-read-path
features.description: A project's repository identity is resolved off the read path and stored on its projection row, so a snapshot read never runs git. Issue #72.
features.keep: RepositoryIdentityReactor.ts, its service, the 003 fork migration and GitWorkDepth.ts are ours whole, and ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts must keep serving the stored repository_identity_json column instead of resolving an identity on the read path; take upstream for the rest of ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts, then re-apply the stored-column reads on top.

features.name: fm-acp-provider
features.description: First Mate is driven through its ACP door as a configurable ACP agent provider. Issues #78 and #79.
features.keep: Every listed file is the fork's own and upstream has no file at these paths, so keep our side of anything that conflicts here; nothing in these files takes upstream. If upstream adds a file at one of these paths, keep our file and rename upstream's.

features.name: fm-worker-threads
features.description: First Mate workers show up as read-only threads, with the fork's own migration track behind them. Issue #81.
features.keep: AcpAgentWorkerThreadReactor.ts, AcpAgentWorkerSessions.ts, AcpPeerSessions.ts and ForkMigrations.ts are ours whole, and decider.ts must keep our read-only thread handling; take upstream for the rest of decider.ts, then re-apply the read-only rules on top.

features.name: fork-connect-public-env
features.description: The desktop build ships with T3 Connect switched on. A clone with no .env gets .env.example copied to .env before the build spawns, so server.asar and app.asar carry the public Clerk key and relay URL. fork-public-env.ts is the fork's own module and upstream has no file at that path, so its test cannot pass on plain upstream. Issue #137.
features.keep: fork-public-env.ts is ours whole, and the call that copies .env.example to .env before the build spawns survives in build-desktop-artifact.ts, the workflow and the doc; everything else in those files takes upstream.

features.name: fm-worker-thread-model
features.description: A read-only worker thread says which model and thinking level is behind it: a strip where the composer would sit, and badges on the sidebar row. ReadOnlyThreadModel.tsx and readOnlyThreadModel.logic.ts are the fork's own modules and upstream has no file at either path, so the test cannot pass on plain upstream. Issue #135.
features.keep: ReadOnlyThreadModel.tsx and readOnlyThreadModel.logic.ts are ours whole, and the model and thinking level strip and sidebar badges they add survive in ChatView.tsx and Sidebar.tsx; everything else in those files takes upstream.

features.name: fm-fleet-thread-roles
features.description: Fleet threads carry a role. The First Mate thread gets its own sidebar slot and never auto-settles; second mates and workers are labelled under their project.
features.keep: fleetThreads.ts, useStartFirstMateThread.ts and fork migration 8 are ours whole, and the fleetRole and fleetRepo fields, the First Mate sidebar slot, the settlement exception and the single First Mate invariant survive in the files listed; everything else in those files follows upstream.

features.name: fm-fleet-thread-read-only-clear
features.description: The fleet can clear read-only on a second mate's thread with thread.read-only.clear, so the user can type into it. Only the fleet issuer may send it, and only on a fleet-owned, unarchived thread whose fleetRole is second-mate. It records a thread.read-only-cleared event that sets readOnly to false on the thread and its shell row, so it survives a restart and clients update. Nothing makes a thread read-only again. The server advertises fleetThreadReadOnlyClear in its environment capabilities.
features.keep: fleetThreadReadOnlyClear.test.ts is ours whole. The thread.read-only-cleared case survives in threadReducer.test.ts, and the fleetThreadReadOnlyClear assertion survives in ServerEnvironment.test.ts. The thread.read-only.clear command, the thread.read-only-cleared event and payload, and the OrchestrationThread.readOnly comment survive in orchestration.ts; the fleetThreadReadOnlyClear capability survives in environment.ts and ServerEnvironment.ts; readOnlyClearRefusal survives in fleetThreads.ts; the issuer stamp for the command survives in Normalizer.ts; the command case survives in decider.ts; the event case survives in projector.ts, ProjectionPipeline.ts and threadReducer.ts; and the payload re-export survives in Schemas.ts. Everything else in those files takes upstream.

features.name: fm-turn-start-when-busy
features.description: A turn start can ask to wait for an idle thread with whenBusy: "queue", so a supervisor's wake never steers into a turn the person just started. The decider holds it while the thread is busy, starts it in the command that frees the thread after a normal turn end, and drops it with a recorded reason on Stop, a stopped, interrupted or failed session, a failed turn start, archive or delete. It is persisted, so it survives a restart and runs once. The server advertises turnStartWhenBusy in its environment capabilities.
features.keep: deferredTurnStarts.ts, ProjectionThreadDeferredTurnStarts.ts, fork migration 9 and turnStartWhenBusy.integration.test.ts are ours whole. The whenBusy option, the thread.turn-start-deferred and thread.deferred-turn-start-dropped events, the thread.deferred-turn-start.release command and the deferredTurnStarts and pendingTurnStart fields survive in orchestration.ts; the turnStartWhenBusy capability survives in environment.ts and ServerEnvironment.ts; the whenBusy queue branch, the release command case and the decideOrchestrationCommand wrapper that calls followDeferredTurnStarts survive in decider.ts; the projectEvent wrapper that calls projectDeferredTurnStarts survives in projector.ts; the deferred-turn-start table writes and reads survive in ProjectionPipeline.ts and ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts; the startup release loop survives in serverRuntimeStartup.ts; and holdCompletion, getSteers, getTurnInputs and awaitSends survive in TestProviderAdapter.integration.ts. Everything else in those files takes upstream.

features.name: fm-turn-start-when-busy-environment
features.description: A deferred turn start (whenBusy: "queue") can carry an environment. The engine keeps it in memory, never on an event or in the deferred-turn-start table, and hands it to the provider reactor when the deferred turn start runs, so the session spawned or restarted for it gets it, as for a direct start. The deferred turn start records only hasEnvironment. After a restart the environment is gone, so the decider drops it with the environment-lost reason instead of running it without it. The decider asks the engine through DeciderContext, a signed-off exception to pure orchestration. The server advertises turnStartWhenBusyEnvironment in its environment capabilities.
features.keep: TurnEnvironment.ts, DeciderContext.ts and deferredTurnStarts.ts are ours whole, including makeDeferredTurnEnvironments and the environment-lost drop in releaseDeferredTurnStart. The hasEnvironment field and the environment-lost drop reason survive in orchestration.ts; the turnStartWhenBusyEnvironment capability survives in environment.ts and ServerEnvironment.ts; and the deferredTurnEnvironments instance, the DeciderContext it provides around decideOrchestrationCommand and its remember call after the commit survive in OrchestrationEngine.ts. Everything else in those files takes upstream.
features.testName: defers a turn start that carries an environment and starts it when free|after a restart, drops a deferred turn start whose environment died with the process|does not defer a turn start that carries an environment without whenBusy

features.name: fm-turn-start-when-busy-environment-reactor-tests
features.description: The provider reactor tests for fm-turn-start-when-busy-environment: a deferred turn start spawns or restarts its session with its environment, and one on an idle thread applies it like a direct start. The manifest takes one test file per entry, so these tests have their own entry.
features.keep: The three tests named in testName, the setThreadTurnRunning helper and the whenBusy option of dispatchTurn survive in ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts. Everything else in that file takes upstream.
features.testName: a deferred turn start spawns its session with its environment|a deferred turn start restarts a live session for its environment|a turn start that asks to wait applies its environment on an idle thread

features.name: fm-turn-start-when-busy-environment-restart-test
features.description: The startup test for fm-turn-start-when-busy-environment: after a real restart a deferred turn start with an environment is dropped with environment-lost and the one behind it runs. The manifest takes one test file per entry, so this test has its own entry.
features.keep: The test named in testName and the decodeProviderEnvironment helper survive in orphanedProviderSessionStartup.integration.test.ts. Everything else in that file takes upstream.
features.testName: drops a deferred turn start whose environment a restart lost

features.name: fm-turn-start-when-busy-ended-session
features.description: A thread whose session stopped or was interrupted, with no active turn, counts as free for a turn start that asks to queue, so the start runs at once instead of becoming a deferred turn start that no event releases. An errored session stays not free, because a runtime error without a turn id leaves a live turn unnamed. A deferred turn start an older server left on such a thread runs at the next startup, through the startup release loop.
features.keep: deferredTurnStarts.ts is ours whole, including the rule in sessionIsFree that counts a stopped or interrupted session with no active turn as free and an errored session as not free. Upstream has no file at that path, so nothing in it takes upstream.
features.testName: a turn start that asks to queue runs at once on a thread whose session stopped|a turn start that asks to queue waits on a thread whose session errored

features.name: fm-turn-start-when-busy-ended-session-restart-test
features.description: The startup test for fm-turn-start-when-busy-ended-session: a deferred turn start left on a stopped session before a restart runs after it. A testName narrows a single test file, and this test lives in another file, so it has its own entry.
features.keep: The test named in testName survives in orphanedProviderSessionStartup.integration.test.ts. Everything else in that file takes upstream.
features.testName: starts a turn start deferred on a stopped session after a restart
